issue_context.title: `any()` aggregation operator
issue_context.body:
## `any()` aggregation operator

It would be useful if we had an aggregation operator that explicitly states "i don't care which value you pick, just pick one". This could have a marginal performance advantage over choosing an arbitrary aggregation, but the real benefit is semantic. when you put, for example, `min()` in a query, the reader assumes that this particular aggregation was chosen for a reason, but in some cases it doesn't matter, like when multiple identical or non-overlapping series are being aggregated. picking an arbitrary aggregation adds meaningless specificity and can make it harder to understand complex queries, while something like `any()` would remove any false meaning from the expression.
comments: This seems really niche. If values don't matter, you could use `count` or `0*count`.

I like the semantic dimension here. I remember discussions about recording-rule naming, where the aggregation should be part of the name, but then you might propagate something like `min` even if it has no meaning. Having an explicit aggregator for that would defuse the discussion.
I have used count many time for this ; I think it is close enough to the original need, and it reads fine too within promql complex queries.
If you want an arbitrary series there's already `topk(1, expr)`. I think anything added here would have to behave like count, but always return the value 1.
Thanks @alice-sawatzky . We have added a `group()` aggregator. We did not name it `any()` because we do not return any value from the aggregation, but instead a value of 1.

Oh, i'm glad my request inspired a feature, although that's not actually what I was looking for!

I was specifically looking for something that _does_ return a value. My intended use case is for situations where there's multiple values being aggregated and they're either non-overlapping temporally or always expected to be the same, where you want one of the values but you don't care how it's selected.
Unfortunately so far promql is fully deterministic (except IIRC the order of the values which depends on how storage sends data), and adding a any() function would be somehow break that promise.
If you're using the value you should care about how you're calculating it in case they are different. One of min, max, or avg is usually what you want.

@roidelapluie ah, that's a good point. since the only point of `any()` is semantic, it would be perfectly fine to implement it deterministically. for example it could be an alias for `min()`, or whatever aggregation operator is determined to be cheapest.

review_comments: I'd add a comment to make it clear this purposefully does nothing.
